knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The method requires a single fresh cloth for each room or area to stop microorganisms moving between areas.
The method calls for a neutral detergent with no softener and no bleach.
The safer practice is to dry a mop after use, because a damp mop is hard to monitor. No Australian time limit is confirmed in this draft, so the answer does not rely on a number.

practicalCriteria: Learner sets out a sample microfibre kit with labelled bags and one cloth per room, with the set-up matching the rule
Learner states the damp-mop time limit and the laundering rules without prompts, with all rules given
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
stopWorkCriteria: Microfibre is in use in an area without infection prevention approval
A product is used that is not on the approved compatibility list
